scheme.name: Moss
scheme.headline: Blue-yellow-green material color language
scheme.summary: A crisp blue-yellow-green material palette for code interfaces.
scheme.positioning: A crisp blue-yellow-green material line inside HearthCode.
audiences: users who prefer drier color worlds
clean charcoal and paper palette preference

constraints.thermalBaseline: clean charcoal substrate, parchment carriers, restrained bronze chrome, and no full-page brown wash
constraints.primaryHueTriad: oxidized CRT blue, old-warning yellow, and terminal lichen green
constraints.allowWarmPressure: yes, but in disciplined old-warning yellow, olive, and oxidized teal lanes rather than orange heat or full-page sepia
avoid: ui chrome colored like syntax hero accents

taxonomy.description: Machine-readable abstract taxonomy for Moss. This groups families, semantic roles, surfaces, interactions, and variants without referencing any platform token names.

foundation.description: Top-level palette families for Moss as a clean-background material companion to HearthCode. The palette is charcoal-led, parchment-carried, and arranged around authored syntax lanes rather than copied historical mappings.

ground.description: Primary charcoal substrate with almost no visible haze.

carrier.description: Readable parchment carrier neutral for body text and long-lived structure.

shell.description: Raised shell family for layered rails, grouped chrome, and side housing.

slate.description: Warm gray-slate neutral for comments and low-pressure guidance.

spark.description: Clear old-warning yellow family for control flow and directive pressure without Ember-like orange heat.

amber.description: Burnished brass and lacquered-paper family for strings, measured highlights, and dry straw warmth.

voltage.description: Oxidized CRT-blue family for constants and secondary structural jump points.

citron.description: Secondary ochre family for operators, warm separators, and cleaner mustard-metal edges.

jade.description: Terminal lichen, sage, and oxidized patina family for green callable rhythm and blue structural type relief.

chalk.description: Parchment neutral carrier for variables, properties, and parameters, keeping the page rhythmic.

surfaceRules.description: Abstract surface anchors for the Moss concept.

panel.description: Raised document substrate mixed up from canvas toward ink.

gutter.description: Visible but quiet gutter band tuned for faster line scanning.

sidebar.description: Shell anchor for navigation, file rails, and grouped UI housing.

border.description: Sharper structural edge than Hearth, but still subordinate to syntax landmarks.

guidanceRules.description: Abstract guidance tones for the textured Moss direction.

guide.description: Quiet structural rail for indent guides and whitespace hints.

guideActive.description: Raised structural rail for the currently active indent band.

whitespace.description: Dormant whitespace cue aligned with the quiet guide rail.

bracketWarm.description: Primary hot bracket rung tied to the live accent band.

bracketBright.description: Secondary bracket rung that adds a quiet oxidized structural accent on light surfaces.

bracketCool.description: Cool bracket rung that keeps nested structure distinct from warm pressure.

bracketMatchFill.description: Soft bracket-match wash built from the primary bracket rung.

bracketMatchStroke.description: Bracket-match stroke emphasis built from the same warm rung with a stronger edge.

guideInk.description: Readable guidance ink for the active line number and focused scaffold labels.

terminalRules.description: Abstract terminal palette for the Moss concept.

ansiRed.description: Terminal failure and destructive hot signal.

ansiMagenta.description: Terminal secondary accent with warmer edge.

ansiCyan.description: Terminal connective cool accent between info and success.

ansiBrightBlack.description: Raised neutral used for muted terminal structure.

interfaceRules.description: Abstract interface tones for material editorial Moss with clearer mustard chrome that stays out of the syntax hero lanes.

shellInk.description: Primary readable shell ink for active tabs, controls, and focused chrome.

supportInk.description: Readable supporting shell ink for general navigation copy.

mutedInk.description: Secondary shell ink for inactive labels and quieter navigation copy.

subtleInk.description: Dormant shell ink for placeholders and low-attention iconography.

onAccentInk.description: Dark charcoal ink for the warm ochre chrome fills (badges, VS Code buttons, web accent chips) that stay bright in both polarities, clearing 4.5:1. Obsidian's --text-on-accent is NOT taken from here: its accent fill is the deep sage, so its on-accent ink is derived per variant by luminance in generate-obsidian-themes.mjs.

shellRaised.description: Raised shell substrate for secondary buttons and grouped controls.

navActiveFill.description: Selected navigation fill for active rows and active tabs.

navInactiveFill.description: Softer navigation fill for inactive hover groups and passive grouping.

shellBand.description: Intermediate shell band for grouped chrome strata and side sections.

accentHoverFill.description: Hover-stage accent fill for buttons and raised controls.

onStatusInk.description: Charcoal ink placed on the persistent amber status band, matching the on-accent treatment so status text clears 4.5:1.

onDeepFillInk.description: Readable light ink for status fills that stay deep-toned in both polarities (no-folder and debugging states).

navActiveInk.description: Readable ink placed on active navigation fills.

interactionRules.description: Abstract interaction primitives for Moss with warm ochre chrome, sage cursor relief, and lower-pressure emphasis.

cursor.description: Primary live cursor and active relief signal. Anchored at the authored sage tone; solved so it stays a visible UI element (WCAG non-text 3:1) against the canvas, and re-solves if the canvas ever shifts under it.

status.description: Persistent emphasis band used for status presence and release accents. Anchored at the authored amber tone; solved so the charcoal status ink clears 4.5:1.

focusRing.description: Focusable edge signal used for ring and border emphasis. Dark follows tabEmphasis; light is deepened so the composited ring clears 3:1 over the editor page.

lineEmphasis.description: Current-line substrate emphasis without becoming a spotlight.

listHover.description: Hover substrate for navigational lists and tabs.

feedbackRules.description: Abstract feedback roles for the Moss concept.

note.description: Calm contextual note and low-pressure explanatory signal.

info.description: Cool informational signal for guidance and neutral notices.

warning.description: Measured caution signal with brighter urgency than Hearth.

error.description: High-urgency failure signal with spark pressure.

semanticRules.description: Semantic role derivation rules for Moss's material editorial direction with authored lane spacing.

variantKnobs.description: Scheme-level variant knobs for the textured Moss direction. Values preserve dusty structure instead of modern accent pressure.

variantProfiles.description: Variant climate profiles. These describe intent and contrast texture, not platform mappings.

semanticRows.note: Charcoal substrate vs dry parchment carrier
Brass connective symbols with low noise
Teal-green method calls for secondary action
Calm olive literals for reading rhythm

colorContract.atmosphere: Textured waste-terminal material with clear instrument signals.

oldWarningYellow.description: Control pressure should read as old-warning yellow, not mud gold or Ember orange.

agedLichenTag.description: Tags should keep old-warning pressure while leaning into aged lichen so they remain distinct from parchment, strings, and control flow.

terminalLichenGreen.description: Callable structure should read as terminal lichen green without becoming generic neon.

sagePropertyStructure.description: Object fields and member structure should carry a quieter sage green presence so Moss reads as structured growth, not neutral parchment.

oxidizedMethodBridge.description: Methods should bridge callable green and oxidized blue so high-frequency calls add rhythm without collapsing into keyword yellow or type blue.

oxidizedCrtBlue.description: Types and numbers should hold the cool structural lane.

lacqueredPaperString.description: Strings should feel like faded lacquered paper or reed-straw, separate from keyword yellow and method green.

oxidizedStructuralPunctuation.description: Punctuation should be a low-weight dry oxide accent that adds light-theme rhythm without becoming a fourth headline lane.

antiGoals: blue becoming a second full foreground
materialRules: Keep charcoal, parchment, and oxidized metal stable while adjusting syntax clarity.
Age belongs mainly to surface and material; syntax lanes must stay crisp.
Use punctuation as a low-weight structural accent, not as a dominant semantic color.

releaseQuality.description: Moss release candidates must be explainable by generated evidence, not only visual preference.

vscodeChromeContract.description: Migrated VS Code workbench chrome bindings sourced from abstract surfaces and interaction primitives. These bindings cover the highest-signal platform colors while token scope baselines remain temporary migration anchors.
